Weekly Student Success and Attendance Meeting Minutes

1. Meeting Overview - it's changed now and update twice

  • Date: 30 September 2026

  • Title: Weekly Student Success and Attendance Meeting

  • Purpose/Objective of the meeting: To address student chronic absenteeism, review seasonal health measures, and coordinate support for individual student welfare.

3. Executive Summary

The meeting focused on addressing a rising trend in student Friday absenteeism and preparing for the upcoming flu season [0-3]. The committee agreed to trial an attendance incentive initiative and launch a health awareness campaign [2-3]. Additionally, a support plan was established for a chronically absent middle school student, John Smith, involving immediate guidance counselling and the sourcing of community childcare support for his family [4-7].

4. Discussion Points

Friday Absenteeism and Attendance Incentives

  • Speaker 1 highlighted a worrying trend of high Friday absenteeism among chronically absent students [0].

  • Speaker 2 reported feedback from mentees indicating they struggle to wake up and attend school on Fridays [1].

  • To address this, Speaker 2 proposed organising a Friday pancake breakfast to incentivise attendance [1]. The committee agreed to pilot this initiative next week [2].

Seasonal Sickness and Hygiene Awareness

  • Speaker 3 noted an increase in seasonal illness (coughing and sniffling) as weather temperatures drop [3].

  • To mitigate the spread of illness ahead of the flu season, the committee discussed the need for preventive measures [3].

  • It was agreed that informational posters promoting basic hygiene practises, such as thorough handwashing, would be displayed across the school to remind both students and teachers [3-4].

Individual Student Case: John Smith

  • Speaker 1 raised the case of John Smith, a middle school student who has already recorded seven absences [4-6].

  • Speaker 2 shared context from a recent conversation with John, noting that he is highly stressed due to childcare responsibilities for his younger siblings during the day [5].

  • Speaker 4 (Guidance Counsellor) offered to meet with John today to provide emotional support and guidance [5-6].

  • Speaker 5 offered to research free or low-cost childcare resources within the local community to assist John's family, reducing his childcare burden so he can return to school [7].

5. Key Decisions

  • Friday Pancake Breakfast Trial: Approved the launch of a Friday pancake breakfast initiative next week to boost attendance [1-2].

  • Hygiene Awareness Campaign: Decided to create and display hygiene posters to prevent the spread of seasonal illnesses [3-4].

  • Support Plan for John Smith: Agreed to a dual-approach support plan involving immediate school counselling and the provision of community childcare resources to his family [5-6][7].

6. Action Items

  • Organise and host the trial Friday pancake breakfast next week (Assigned to: Speaker 2) [1-2]

  • Design and display hygiene promotion posters across the school (Assigned to: Speaker 3) [3-4]

  • Meet with student John Smith today to discuss his current stressors and provide guidance counsellor support (Assigned to: Speaker 4) [5-6]

  • Research and compile free or low-cost community childcare resources for John Smith's family (Assigned to: Speaker 5) [7]

  • Share the compiled childcare resources with John Smith so he can pass them to his family (Assigned to: Speaker 5) [7]

7. Next Steps

  • Monitor the impact of the Friday pancake breakfast on weekly attendance levels [1-2]

  • Review John Smith's attendance and welfare status at the next weekly meeting [4-7]

  • Assess the rollout of the seasonal hygiene posters and teacher engagement [3-4]
